'''Patricia Gabbey Gensel''' (born March 18, 1944) is an American [[Botany|botanist]] and [[Paleobotany|paleobotanist]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kiki.huh.harvard.edu/databases/botanist_search.php?id=77625|title=HUH - Databases - Botanist Search}}</ref><ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=https://bio.unc.edu/people/faculty/gensel/|title=Patricia G. Gensel|date=April 28, 2011 }}</ref>

==Life==
Gensel was born in [[Buffalo, New York]], and attended [[Hope College]] in [[Holland, Michigan]], earning a B.A. in 1966.<ref name="Who's Who 1983">{{cite book|contribution=Gensel, Patricia Gabbey|title=Who's Who of American Women, 1983-1984|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Cz2ppa_YfZ8C|date= 1983|publisher=[[Marquis Who's Who]]|isbn=978-0-8379-0413-9|page=284}}</ref> She obtained her [[Ph.D.]] in 1972 from the [[University of Connecticut]]. Until her retirement in 2024, Gensel was on the faculty of the Biology Department of the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].<ref name=bio />

Gensel is noted for her research on [[Paleozoic]] plants.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.colorado.edu/eeb/MORPH/MORPH/Labs_-_Patricia_G._Gensel.html|title=Labs - Patricia G. Gensel|access-date=2016-04-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402092224/http://www.colorado.edu/eeb/MORPH/MORPH/Labs_-_Patricia_G._Gensel.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}}</ref> She served as president of the [[Botanical Society of America]] for 2000–2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://botany.org/newsite/reporting/mail/f04officers.pdf|title=Botany.org (pdf)|website=botany.org|access-date=April 9, 2016|archive-date=August 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811194939/http://www.botany.org/newsite/reporting/mail/f04officers.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Gensel is the namesake of the genus, ''Genselia'' Knaus, which consists of four species of early [[Carboniferous]] plants found in the Pocono and Price Formations in the [[Geology of the Appalachians|Appalachian Basin]] of North America.<ref>{{cite journal|jstor=2474900|title=The Species of the Early Carboniferous Fossil Plant Genus Genselia|journal=International Journal of Plant Sciences|volume=156|issue=1|pages=61–92|last1=Knaus|first1=Margaret Jane|year=1995|doi=10.1086/297230|s2cid=83629753}}</ref>
